source_solver: Gurobi 13.0.3 via gurobipy (size-limited pip licence), original notebook code cells for the default variant 'S' run unmodified (only the %pip line and the plotting cell dropped) on 2026-10-02
notes: Gurobi reports NumVars 72, NumConstrs 25, NumIntVars 0, no quadratic or general constraints; ObjVal 1.5662499999999997, which is exactly 1.56625 = 2.66 export revenue - 1.09375 import cost. The objective is unique, and so are the aggregate plan numbers (7.8125 kWh bought, 7.2 kWh sold, revenue 2.66, cost 1.09375, final stored energy 6, peak stored energy 13.5), checked by maximising and minimising each over the optimal face. The hourly timing has alternative optima: charging can be split freely over 02-03 and 03-04 (both 0.14 per kWh; Gurobi 2.8125/5.0, HiGHS 2.8125/5.0, SCIP 5.0/2.8125) and the 2.2 kWh sold at 0.30 can sit in any of 19-20, 20-21, 22-23, 23-24 (Gurobi 20-21, HiGHS and SCIP 19-20); so only totals and the profit are scored. Same formulation and size as the notebook's S model (24 hourly steps; charge, discharge and stored-energy variables with bounds; 24 stored-energy balances plus one terminal-charge constraint). Differences, none of which changes the instance: the notebook passes a single power bound Pmax_kw (set to its charge limit, 5 kW) for both charging and discharging, whereas here max_charge_kw and max_discharge_kw are separate parameters holding the notebook's published P_ch_max_kw and P_dis_max_kw (both 5.0); the notebook's dt_h = 1.0 is the column hours.step_hours (structural, not editable). Not ported: variant LG (load minus PV settled at the tariff, closed form, no optimisation) and variant LGS (adds load, PV, import and export variables and a nonlinear power-law cycling cost with exponent beta = 1.5, so not an LP; the fetched notebook contains no indicator constraints). The load and PV profiles, kappa_cyc and beta are used only by LG and LGS, so they are not part of this model's data.
